data.title: Fiscal 2026 overview
data.conclusion: NVIDIA's fiscal 2026 filing reports [[ref:revenue,period:2026FY,text:Revenue of $215.938 billion]] and [[ref:net_profit,period:2026FY,text:Net profit attributable to shareholders of $120.067 billion]]. Operating cash flow was $102.718 billion.
data.evidence: The annual financial tables report [[ref:gross_margin,period:2026FY,text:Gross margin of 71.07%]] and a period-end [[ref:debt_to_asset,period:2026FY,text:Debt-to-asset ratio of 23.94%]].; The filing says Blackwell architectures represented the majority of Data Center sales, identifying the principal operating driver behind the annual scale.
data.cross_checks: The annual income statement figures agree with the filing's management discussion. The fiscal-year cash-flow figure agrees with its liquidity discussion.
data.counterpoints: The annual result should not be confused with a derived single-quarter observation. Data Center concentration and the transition to full-scale systems affect how durable these results may be.
data.investor_implication: The starting point is strong annual earnings and cash generation, but product concentration and system economics deserve separate scrutiny.

data.title: Quarterly trend and turning points
data.conclusion: The available 12-quarter history shows sustained expansion in derived quarterly sales through 2026Q4, but uneven quarterly cash conversion.
data.evidence: Derived [[ref:revenue,period:2026Q4,compare_period:2025Q4,text:2026Q4 Revenue was $68.127 billion versus $39.331 billion in 2025Q4]]. Derived [[ref:net_profit,period:2026Q4,compare_period:2025Q4,text:2026Q4 Net profit attributable to shareholders was $42.960 billion versus $22.091 billion in 2025Q4]].; The 2026Q4 operating cash-flow observation was $36.188 billion, compared with $23.751 billion in 2026Q3; both are derived single-quarter flows.
data.cross_checks: The 2026Q4 sales observation equals the fiscal-year total less the nine-month cumulative figure; the same subtraction applies to profit and operating cash flow.; The filing attributes annual growth to Data Center computing and networking, consistent with the direction of the quarterly sales series.
data.counterpoints: Only the year-end annual gross-margin ratio and period-end leverage ratio are available in this quarterly series; neither establishes a quarter-by-quarter ratio trend.; The supplied quarterly labels are retained as given, although their synthetic calendar dates do not align with the January 2026 fiscal-year end stated in the filing.
data.investor_implication: Use the quarterly flows to assess momentum, while keeping them distinct from full-year results and treating the supplied quarter-date mapping cautiously.

data.title: Growth quality
data.conclusion: Growth is supported by actual Data Center platform sales, but is highly concentrated by product and customer.
data.evidence: The annual product table assigns $193.737 billion, or 89.72% of total sales, to Data Center products; gaming GPUs and related products account for $16.042 billion.; The filing reports 59% growth in Data Center computing and 142% growth in Data Center networking, associated with Blackwell demand and the NVLink fabric ramp.; Two direct customers represented 22% and 14% of fiscal 2026 sales, respectively.
data.cross_checks: The product mix agrees directionally with management's statement that Blackwell architectures represented the majority of Data Center sales.; The filing's Compute & Networking segment is not identical to the Data Center product category, so their totals should not be substituted for each other.
data.counterpoints: Sales to direct customers do not identify ultimate end-user demand; indirect-customer exposure is estimated by management.; The available product table does not isolate GPU or AI-chip sales from networking, systems, software and other Data Center offerings.
data.investor_implication: Monitor large-customer spending and the mix of compute, networking and complete systems rather than treating aggregate growth as diversified.

data.title: Profitability quality
data.conclusion: [[ref:gross_margin,period:2026FY,text:Fiscal 2026 Gross margin was 71.07%]], but the filing reports a decline from 75.0% in fiscal 2025.
data.evidence: Management attributes the decline to a shift from Hopper HGX systems toward Blackwell full-scale Data Center solutions and a $4.5 billion H20 excess-inventory and purchase-obligation charge.; Fiscal 2026 inventory and excess-purchase-obligation provisions totaled $7.2 billion, partly offset by $1.5 billion of provision releases; management reports a net adverse margin effect of 2.6 percentage points.; Research and development expense was $18.497 billion, up from $12.914 billion, as compensation and compute infrastructure spending rose.
data.cross_checks: The annual product table's $153.463 billion of gross profit on $215.938 billion of sales reconciles to the reported margin.; The filing reports $9.022 billion of other income, net, primarily affected by investment gains; this is distinct from core operating performance.
data.counterpoints: The supplied series lacks comparable quarterly gross-margin observations, and the annual margin decline cannot be assigned to a particular quarter.; Removing the H20 charge alone would not establish a sustainable margin for the newer system mix.
data.investor_implication: Track the economics of complete systems, inventory provisions and investment-related gains separately when assessing repeatable profitability.

data.title: Profit and cash consistency
data.conclusion: Fiscal 2026 operating cash flow of $102.718 billion covered about 85.6% of [[ref:net_profit,period:2026FY,text:Net profit attributable to shareholders of $120.067 billion]]; cash generation was substantial but below accounting profit.
data.evidence: The Cash flow statement reports investing cash flow of negative $52.228 billion and financing cash flow of negative $48.474 billion.; The filing reports $6.1 billion of capital expenditures and says the increase in investing cash outflow was primarily driven by equity-security purchases and a non-exclusive Groq license agreement.; Management says higher share repurchases were the main reason financing cash outflow increased from fiscal 2025.
data.cross_checks: Reported operating cash flow increased from $64.089 billion in fiscal 2025; management attributes the increase to higher sales.; Fiscal 2026 capital expenditure is not equivalent to the much larger net investing cash outflow.
data.counterpoints: Investment-related unrealized gains contributed to other income; net profit therefore contains items that need not produce operating cash in the same period.; The supplied figures do not provide a complete working-capital bridge, so the profit-to-cash difference cannot be allocated precisely.
data.investor_implication: Evaluate cash conversion alongside investment gains, working capital and actual capital expenditure, rather than using the investing cash-flow total as a capital-spending proxy.

data.title: Balance sheet pressure
data.conclusion: The year-end [[ref:debt_to_asset,period:2026FY,text:Debt-to-asset ratio was 23.94%]]; immediate financing pressure appears limited, while supply commitments and strategic exposures merit attention.
data.evidence: The Balance sheet figures show $206.803 billion of assets, $49.510 billion of liabilities and $10.605 billion of cash and cash equivalents.; The filing adds $51.951 billion of marketable securities, bringing cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities to $62.556 billion; senior notes had an approximately $8.5 billion carrying amount.; Management reports $3.5 billion of land, power and shell guarantees to early-stage companies, generally over multi-year periods.
data.cross_checks: The reported leverage ratio is consistent with total liabilities divided by total assets.; The filing says no commercial paper was outstanding at its fiscal-year end, despite an authorized issuance program.
data.counterpoints: Cash equivalents alone omit marketable securities; conversely, not all securities or private investments have the same liquidity and valuation characteristics.; Guarantees and non-cancellable supply orders create risks not captured by the headline leverage ratio.
data.investor_implication: Assess liquidity together with securities composition, guarantees, supply commitments and the pace of shareholder returns.

data.title: Unknowns and limits
data.conclusion: The annual filing supports a fiscal 2026 operating assessment, but the supplied quarterly chronology and post-filing observations cannot be reconciled into a reliable subsequent-results narrative.
data.evidence: The filing identifies its fiscal-year end as January 25, 2026 and its filing date is February 25, 2026. The supplied quarterly series nevertheless assigns 2026Q4 a December 31, 2026 report date.; The available 12-quarter history contains derived quarterly sales, profit and operating cash flows, but almost no quarterly margin or leverage observations.; Later-dated operating tables and a forecast are present in the evidence bundle; they are not treated as fiscal 2026 annual results or as confirmation of the filing's plans.
data.cross_checks: The annual totals match the fiscal-year filing, while the derived quarterly values arithmetically reconcile to the cumulative financial tables. Arithmetic agreement does not resolve the conflicting dates.
data.counterpoints: Product-category figures do not separately establish AI-chip unit volumes, pricing or GPU-only sales; annual inventory turnover and an annual inventory balance are not supplied here.; The filing discusses future product shipments and capital spending, but the supplied evidence does not establish whether those plans were subsequently achieved.
data.investor_implication: Anchor conclusions to the filed annual period and label quarterly calculations as supplied, without interpreting their dates as a verified post-filing timeline.

data.title: Business outlook
data.conclusion: NVIDIA enters its next product cycle from a large, profitable fiscal 2026 base: [[ref:revenue,period:2026FY,text:Revenue was $215.938 billion]], operating cash flow was $102.718 billion, and Data Center products accounted for 89.72% of annual sales in the supplied product table. The investment case rests less on an undifferentiated AI market forecast than on whether NVIDIA can deliver successive rack-scale platforms, secure constrained components and customer infrastructure, and preserve attractive economics as complete-system sales grow. These are execution questions, not achieved future results.
data.evidence: The filing says Blackwell architectures represented the majority of fiscal 2026 Data Center sales. Blackwell Ultra production units, including GB300, began shipping in the second quarter of fiscal 2026. NVIDIA describes a one-year cadence for advanced Data Center architectures and expects Rubin production shipments to begin in the second half of fiscal 2027. That Rubin timing is a company expectation, not a reported shipment outcome.; Demand has an observable operating base: management attributes fiscal 2026 growth to Data Center compute and networking, including demand for Blackwell computing and a ramp in NVLink fabric for GB200 and GB300. Its platform combines GPUs, CPUs, networking and software; CUDA, AI Enterprise and developer adoption may support integration across training and inference. Two direct customers accounted for 22% and 14% of annual sales, however, and significant indirect demand depends on a limited group of buyers.; Customer deployment also depends on data-center sites, electricity and financing. Management warns that energy expansion is a complex, multi-year process and less-capitalized builders may struggle to fund infrastructure. The company reported $3.5 billion of multi-year land, power and shell guarantees to early-stage partners. Those arrangements support prospective build-outs but also expose NVIDIA to partner defaults.; On supply, NVIDIA uses external foundries, memory vendors, packaging providers and contract manufacturers. Its supply chain remains mainly concentrated in Asia, although it is expanding relationships in the United States and Latin America. Management says some manufacturing lead times exceed twelve months and it may place non-cancellable orders, pay premiums or make deposits to reserve capacity. The fiscal 2026 H20-related $4.5 billion charge shows how quickly regulatory changes can impair inventory and purchase commitments.
data.cross_checks: The supplied product table's Data Center share and the filing's account of Blackwell-led growth reinforce the operating baseline, but the table does not disclose GPU-only or AI-chip-only sales. The annual filing reports $18.497 billion of research and development expense and $6.1 billion of capital expenditures; management expects capital expenditures to increase in fiscal 2027. That expectation is not evidence of spending already incurred.; Cash allocation is consequential alongside the roadmap: NVIDIA reports $40.4 billion of fiscal 2026 share repurchases and $17.5 billion invested in private companies and infrastructure funds. Some investees buy NVIDIA products directly or through cloud providers, making customer financing and investment returns relevant to demand quality. A proposed OpenAI investment and partnership remained under negotiation in the filing, with no assurance of completion.
data.counterpoints: The company says export controls effectively foreclosed it from China's Data Center compute market at fiscal 2026 year-end. H20 licenses produced about $60 million of sales; a later H200 license covered only small quantities for specified customers, with no sales reported under that program at the filing's stated point in time. Whether China permits imports, whether tariffs can be passed through, and the scope of replacement U.S. export rules remain uncertain. Customer-headquarters geography is not the same as end-market exposure.; The move from Hopper HGX systems to Blackwell full-scale solutions coincided with a decline in [[ref:gross_margin,period:2026FY,text:fiscal 2026 Gross margin to 71.07%]]. Product transitions can introduce yield, quality, inventory and warranty costs, while cloud providers and chip suppliers develop alternatives. Gaming supply constraints were expected to remain a headwind into fiscal 2027. The supplied quarterly dates conflict with the filing's fiscal-year end, so they cannot verify later roadmap milestones.
data.investor_implication: Monitor confirmed Rubin shipment timing, Blackwell system mix and margin, networking adoption, customer concentration, power and funding availability, and inventory commitments. Compare operating cash generation with repurchases, capital spending, investments and guarantees. Strong current demand supports investment in the platform, but neither proposed transactions nor planned capacity and products should be capitalized into an achieved growth trajectory without subsequent, consistently dated results.

cards.title: Fiscal 2026 overview
cards.conclusion: NVIDIA's fiscal 2026 filing reports [[ref:revenue,period:2026FY,text:Revenue of $215.938 billion]] and [[ref:net_profit,period:2026FY,text:Net profit attributable to shareholders of $120.067 billion]]. Operating cash flow was $102.718 billion.
cards.evidence: The annual financial tables report [[ref:gross_margin,period:2026FY,text:Gross margin of 71.07%]] and a period-end [[ref:debt_to_asset,period:2026FY,text:Debt-to-asset ratio of 23.94%]].; The filing says Blackwell architectures represented the majority of Data Center sales, identifying the principal operating driver behind the annual scale.
cards.cross_checks: The annual income statement figures agree with the filing's management discussion. The fiscal-year cash-flow figure agrees with its liquidity discussion.
cards.counterpoints: The annual result should not be confused with a derived single-quarter observation. Data Center concentration and the transition to full-scale systems affect how durable these results may be.
cards.investor_implication: The starting point is strong annual earnings and cash generation, but product concentration and system economics deserve separate scrutiny.

cards.title: Quarterly trend and turning points
cards.conclusion: The available 12-quarter history shows sustained expansion in derived quarterly sales through 2026Q4, but uneven quarterly cash conversion.
cards.evidence: Derived [[ref:revenue,period:2026Q4,compare_period:2025Q4,text:2026Q4 Revenue was $68.127 billion versus $39.331 billion in 2025Q4]]. Derived [[ref:net_profit,period:2026Q4,compare_period:2025Q4,text:2026Q4 Net profit attributable to shareholders was $42.960 billion versus $22.091 billion in 2025Q4]].; The 2026Q4 operating cash-flow observation was $36.188 billion, compared with $23.751 billion in 2026Q3; both are derived single-quarter flows.
cards.cross_checks: The 2026Q4 sales observation equals the fiscal-year total less the nine-month cumulative figure; the same subtraction applies to profit and operating cash flow.; The filing attributes annual growth to Data Center computing and networking, consistent with the direction of the quarterly sales series.
cards.counterpoints: Only the year-end annual gross-margin ratio and period-end leverage ratio are available in this quarterly series; neither establishes a quarter-by-quarter ratio trend.; The supplied quarterly labels are retained as given, although their synthetic calendar dates do not align with the January 2026 fiscal-year end stated in the filing.
cards.investor_implication: Use the quarterly flows to assess momentum, while keeping them distinct from full-year results and treating the supplied quarter-date mapping cautiously.

cards.title: Growth quality
cards.conclusion: Growth is supported by actual Data Center platform sales, but is highly concentrated by product and customer.
cards.evidence: The annual product table assigns $193.737 billion, or 89.72% of total sales, to Data Center products; gaming GPUs and related products account for $16.042 billion.; The filing reports 59% growth in Data Center computing and 142% growth in Data Center networking, associated with Blackwell demand and the NVLink fabric ramp.; Two direct customers represented 22% and 14% of fiscal 2026 sales, respectively.
cards.cross_checks: The product mix agrees directionally with management's statement that Blackwell architectures represented the majority of Data Center sales.; The filing's Compute & Networking segment is not identical to the Data Center product category, so their totals should not be substituted for each other.
cards.counterpoints: Sales to direct customers do not identify ultimate end-user demand; indirect-customer exposure is estimated by management.; The available product table does not isolate GPU or AI-chip sales from networking, systems, software and other Data Center offerings.
cards.investor_implication: Monitor large-customer spending and the mix of compute, networking and complete systems rather than treating aggregate growth as diversified.

cards.title: Profitability quality
cards.conclusion: [[ref:gross_margin,period:2026FY,text:Fiscal 2026 Gross margin was 71.07%]], but the filing reports a decline from 75.0% in fiscal 2025.
cards.evidence: Management attributes the decline to a shift from Hopper HGX systems toward Blackwell full-scale Data Center solutions and a $4.5 billion H20 excess-inventory and purchase-obligation charge.; Fiscal 2026 inventory and excess-purchase-obligation provisions totaled $7.2 billion, partly offset by $1.5 billion of provision releases; management reports a net adverse margin effect of 2.6 percentage points.; Research and development expense was $18.497 billion, up from $12.914 billion, as compensation and compute infrastructure spending rose.
cards.cross_checks: The annual product table's $153.463 billion of gross profit on $215.938 billion of sales reconciles to the reported margin.; The filing reports $9.022 billion of other income, net, primarily affected by investment gains; this is distinct from core operating performance.
cards.counterpoints: The supplied series lacks comparable quarterly gross-margin observations, and the annual margin decline cannot be assigned to a particular quarter.; Removing the H20 charge alone would not establish a sustainable margin for the newer system mix.
cards.investor_implication: Track the economics of complete systems, inventory provisions and investment-related gains separately when assessing repeatable profitability.

cards.title: Profit and cash consistency
cards.conclusion: Fiscal 2026 operating cash flow of $102.718 billion covered about 85.6% of [[ref:net_profit,period:2026FY,text:Net profit attributable to shareholders of $120.067 billion]]; cash generation was substantial but below accounting profit.
cards.evidence: The Cash flow statement reports investing cash flow of negative $52.228 billion and financing cash flow of negative $48.474 billion.; The filing reports $6.1 billion of capital expenditures and says the increase in investing cash outflow was primarily driven by equity-security purchases and a non-exclusive Groq license agreement.; Management says higher share repurchases were the main reason financing cash outflow increased from fiscal 2025.
cards.cross_checks: Reported operating cash flow increased from $64.089 billion in fiscal 2025; management attributes the increase to higher sales.; Fiscal 2026 capital expenditure is not equivalent to the much larger net investing cash outflow.
cards.counterpoints: Investment-related unrealized gains contributed to other income; net profit therefore contains items that need not produce operating cash in the same period.; The supplied figures do not provide a complete working-capital bridge, so the profit-to-cash difference cannot be allocated precisely.
cards.investor_implication: Evaluate cash conversion alongside investment gains, working capital and actual capital expenditure, rather than using the investing cash-flow total as a capital-spending proxy.

cards.title: Balance sheet pressure
cards.conclusion: The year-end [[ref:debt_to_asset,period:2026FY,text:Debt-to-asset ratio was 23.94%]]; immediate financing pressure appears limited, while supply commitments and strategic exposures merit attention.
cards.evidence: The Balance sheet figures show $206.803 billion of assets, $49.510 billion of liabilities and $10.605 billion of cash and cash equivalents.; The filing adds $51.951 billion of marketable securities, bringing cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities to $62.556 billion; senior notes had an approximately $8.5 billion carrying amount.; Management reports $3.5 billion of land, power and shell guarantees to early-stage companies, generally over multi-year periods.
cards.cross_checks: The reported leverage ratio is consistent with total liabilities divided by total assets.; The filing says no commercial paper was outstanding at its fiscal-year end, despite an authorized issuance program.
cards.counterpoints: Cash equivalents alone omit marketable securities; conversely, not all securities or private investments have the same liquidity and valuation characteristics.; Guarantees and non-cancellable supply orders create risks not captured by the headline leverage ratio.
cards.investor_implication: Assess liquidity together with securities composition, guarantees, supply commitments and the pace of shareholder returns.

cards.title: Unknowns and limits
cards.conclusion: The annual filing supports a fiscal 2026 operating assessment, but the supplied quarterly chronology and post-filing observations cannot be reconciled into a reliable subsequent-results narrative.
cards.evidence: The filing identifies its fiscal-year end as January 25, 2026 and its filing date is February 25, 2026. The supplied quarterly series nevertheless assigns 2026Q4 a December 31, 2026 report date.; The available 12-quarter history contains derived quarterly sales, profit and operating cash flows, but almost no quarterly margin or leverage observations.; Later-dated operating tables and a forecast are present in the evidence bundle; they are not treated as fiscal 2026 annual results or as confirmation of the filing's plans.
cards.cross_checks: The annual totals match the fiscal-year filing, while the derived quarterly values arithmetically reconcile to the cumulative financial tables. Arithmetic agreement does not resolve the conflicting dates.
cards.counterpoints: Product-category figures do not separately establish AI-chip unit volumes, pricing or GPU-only sales; annual inventory turnover and an annual inventory balance are not supplied here.; The filing discusses future product shipments and capital spending, but the supplied evidence does not establish whether those plans were subsequently achieved.
cards.investor_implication: Anchor conclusions to the filed annual period and label quarterly calculations as supplied, without interpreting their dates as a verified post-filing timeline.

cards.title: Business outlook
cards.conclusion: NVIDIA enters its next product cycle from a large, profitable fiscal 2026 base: [[ref:revenue,period:2026FY,text:Revenue was $215.938 billion]], operating cash flow was $102.718 billion, and Data Center products accounted for 89.72% of annual sales in the supplied product table. The investment case rests less on an undifferentiated AI market forecast than on whether NVIDIA can deliver successive rack-scale platforms, secure constrained components and customer infrastructure, and preserve attractive economics as complete-system sales grow. These are execution questions, not achieved future results.
cards.evidence: The filing says Blackwell architectures represented the majority of fiscal 2026 Data Center sales. Blackwell Ultra production units, including GB300, began shipping in the second quarter of fiscal 2026. NVIDIA describes a one-year cadence for advanced Data Center architectures and expects Rubin production shipments to begin in the second half of fiscal 2027. That Rubin timing is a company expectation, not a reported shipment outcome.; Demand has an observable operating base: management attributes fiscal 2026 growth to Data Center compute and networking, including demand for Blackwell computing and a ramp in NVLink fabric for GB200 and GB300. Its platform combines GPUs, CPUs, networking and software; CUDA, AI Enterprise and developer adoption may support integration across training and inference. Two direct customers accounted for 22% and 14% of annual sales, however, and significant indirect demand depends on a limited group of buyers.; Customer deployment also depends on data-center sites, electricity and financing. Management warns that energy expansion is a complex, multi-year process and less-capitalized builders may struggle to fund infrastructure. The company reported $3.5 billion of multi-year land, power and shell guarantees to early-stage partners. Those arrangements support prospective build-outs but also expose NVIDIA to partner defaults.; On supply, NVIDIA uses external foundries, memory vendors, packaging providers and contract manufacturers. Its supply chain remains mainly concentrated in Asia, although it is expanding relationships in the United States and Latin America. Management says some manufacturing lead times exceed twelve months and it may place non-cancellable orders, pay premiums or make deposits to reserve capacity. The fiscal 2026 H20-related $4.5 billion charge shows how quickly regulatory changes can impair inventory and purchase commitments.
cards.cross_checks: The supplied product table's Data Center share and the filing's account of Blackwell-led growth reinforce the operating baseline, but the table does not disclose GPU-only or AI-chip-only sales. The annual filing reports $18.497 billion of research and development expense and $6.1 billion of capital expenditures; management expects capital expenditures to increase in fiscal 2027. That expectation is not evidence of spending already incurred.; Cash allocation is consequential alongside the roadmap: NVIDIA reports $40.4 billion of fiscal 2026 share repurchases and $17.5 billion invested in private companies and infrastructure funds. Some investees buy NVIDIA products directly or through cloud providers, making customer financing and investment returns relevant to demand quality. A proposed OpenAI investment and partnership remained under negotiation in the filing, with no assurance of completion.
cards.counterpoints: The company says export controls effectively foreclosed it from China's Data Center compute market at fiscal 2026 year-end. H20 licenses produced about $60 million of sales; a later H200 license covered only small quantities for specified customers, with no sales reported under that program at the filing's stated point in time. Whether China permits imports, whether tariffs can be passed through, and the scope of replacement U.S. export rules remain uncertain. Customer-headquarters geography is not the same as end-market exposure.; The move from Hopper HGX systems to Blackwell full-scale solutions coincided with a decline in [[ref:gross_margin,period:2026FY,text:fiscal 2026 Gross margin to 71.07%]]. Product transitions can introduce yield, quality, inventory and warranty costs, while cloud providers and chip suppliers develop alternatives. Gaming supply constraints were expected to remain a headwind into fiscal 2027. The supplied quarterly dates conflict with the filing's fiscal-year end, so they cannot verify later roadmap milestones.
cards.investor_implication: Monitor confirmed Rubin shipment timing, Blackwell system mix and margin, networking adoption, customer concentration, power and funding availability, and inventory commitments. Compare operating cash generation with repurchases, capital spending, investments and guarantees. Strong current demand supports investment in the platform, but neither proposed transactions nor planned capacity and products should be capitalized into an achieved growth trajectory without subsequent, consistently dated results.

audit.summary: NVIDIA's fiscal 2026 filing shows a large, profitable Data Center-led business with substantial cash generation. The next test is whether successive complete-system platforms can sustain growth and attractive economics. The filed annual results support a strong operating base, but investment conclusions should rest on verified future results for system margins, customer demand and product shipments, not on the inconsistent quarterly timeline or management plans.

challenge_points.issue: Original claim: The available 12-quarter history shows sustained expansion in derived quarterly sales through 2026Q4, but uneven quarterly cash conversion. Revised view: The supplied 12-quarter calculations rise across their labeled fiscal 2026 quarters and show uneven operating cash flow, but their dates do not establish a valid fiscal 2026 chronology. Treat the derived quarterly figures as provisional calculations, not verified sequential results or evidence of post-filing momentum.. Reason: The fiscal 2026 filing says the year ended January 25, 2026, whereas the supplied series dates its labeled 2026Q1 through 2026Q4 observations from March through December 2026. Arithmetic reconciliation to annual totals does not resolve that time-window conflict.

resolved_points.rationale: The fiscal 2026 annual figures for sales, shareholder profit and operating cash flow agree with the filing and current-period financial data.
The filing supports Blackwell-led Data Center growth and substantial direct-customer concentration. Data Center products and the Compute & Networking operating segment are distinct categories.
The filing supports the annual margin decline, the system-mix shift, inventory charges and higher research spending. It does not establish a quarterly margin trend.
Operating cash flow was substantial but below annual shareholder profit. The card correctly distinguishes capital expenditures from total investing cash outflow.
The year-end balance sheet and liquidity figures support limited immediate financing pressure, while guarantees and supply commitments remain relevant risks.
The card identifies the conflict between the filing's January 2026 fiscal-year end and the supplied quarterly dates, and does not present later plans as completed results.
The filing supports the stated platform, customer, supply and regulatory considerations. Rubin shipments and higher fiscal 2027 capital spending are correctly framed as expectations.
